repairs.value: The AI text combines Sechler’s claim that uncertainty fosters cooperative inquiry and fellowship with Clifton’s insistence that a person must recognize God as an available relational option. It extends both moves by proposing a proportional-access rule: evidential variation is permissible only when sincere seekers retain enough recognizable, actionable access to choose relationship without coercion.

The AI text joins Sechler’s claim that sincere truth-seeking can save without explicit theological assent to Clifton’s objection that punishment for involuntary nonbelief is unjust. It extends those moves into an inclusivist standard that evaluates responsible orientation toward truth and relationship while treating Christianity as salvation’s source without making correct identification a universal entry requirement.
